The provided documentation outlines the installation, configuration, and technical specifications for Strata, a local AI server running the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model. Designed for AI agents, the setup guide emphasizes strict security protocols, mandating that servers remain bound to `127.0.0.1` unless protected by API keys. It details hardware requirements, specifying support for NVIDIA RTX 20-50 series and specific AMD Radeon cards (RX 7900 XT, RX 9070, etc.) with minimum 12GB VRAM and 32GB RAM. The process involves cloning the repository, selecting a model quantization size (e.g., IQ2_XS, IQ3_S) based on available RAM, and executing setup scripts (`START-HERE.bat` on Windows, `setup.sh` on Linux) with flags for non-interactive installation.

The AMD-specific documentation elaborates on the HIP backend, which maps CUDA runtime calls to HIP/hipBLAS for RDNA2/3/4 architectures. On Linux, setup automatically installs ROCm into a virtual environment if system-wide ROCm is absent, compiling the engine for the specific GPU architecture. Windows support, introduced in version 0.1.34, utilizes a pre-built engine zip containing necessary ROCm libraries, requiring only a current AMD driver. Key technical nuances include handling Windows-specific driver conflicts with `amdhip64_7.dll`, managing VRAM budgets via WDDM, and addressing PCIe probe timing issues. The text also notes limitations, such as CPU-only image processing on AMD and single-card constraints on Windows. Finally, it describes the server’s OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible API endpoints, verification steps via `curl`, and troubleshooting guides for common issues like driver mismatches, out-of-memory errors, and download interruptions, ensuring users can deploy a secure, local LLM environment efficiently.
